newsitem.title: LATVIA: LMT STATE SHARE SELL-OFF RULES SET - LPA.
newsitem.headline: LMT STATE SHARE SELL-OFF RULES SET - LPA.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Thursday that it has set rules for the sale of the state's shares in mobile phone operator Latvijas Mobilais Telefons (LMT) to one of the current shareholders, Lattelekom.
"The agency approved the selling of 1,980 parts of the state capital to Lattelekom, which already owns five percent of LMT," Toms Zeikats of LPA told Reuters.
Lattelekom, a monopoly telecommunication's provider, in which Britain's Cable & Wireless and Telecom Finland hold a big stake, will now sign a purchase agreement.
"The concrete sums involved will become clearer as we start working on the sale agreement withinn the next three to four weeks," Zeikats added.
LMT, one of the two mobile phone operators in Latvia, is co-owned by Finland and Sweden's telecom companies, each controlling 24.5 percent of its stake.
